seoTitle: How to Cancel Hostinger VPS, Cloud & Shared Hosting
metaDescription: Cancel a Hostinger VPS, Cloud, or shared hosting subscription the way the billing page is built: disable auto-renewal or cancel outright, and what happens to your data either way.
intro: Every subscription Hostinger bills you for, VPS, Cloud, shared hosting, sits in one place: Billing → Subscriptions. It's the same page whether you're stopping a plan that renews automatically or backing out of an order you never finished paying for. There's no single delete button for a service in hPanel, so the row itself tells you which control applies: an auto-renewal toggle for something still active, or a Cancel subscription action once you're ready to end it for good.
prerequisites: A Hostinger account with at least one active or pending subscription
Any files, databases, or email you need from the service, backed up locally before you cancel

steps.heading: Go to Billing → Subscriptions
steps.body: From hPanel, open Billing and select Subscriptions. The page lists every subscription on the account with its service name, associated domain, billing date, renewal price, and a status of active, pending setup, expired, or cancelled. A banner reading "Auto-renewal will not work" can appear at the top if there's no payment method on file, which means renewals are already paused account-wide until you add one.

image.caption: Billing → Subscriptions, listing each service with its billing date, renewal price, and current status.

steps.heading: Find the specific VPS, Cloud, or shared hosting row
steps.body: Scroll or search the list for the plan you want to act on. A VPS order that was started but never paid for shows as pending setup with a button to complete the order, not an expiration date. An active plan, a running Cloud hosting subscription, for instance, shows a real billing date and its current auto-renewal state. Which state your subscription is in decides which of the next two steps applies to you.

image.caption: Subscription rows in different states: one pending setup, one active with auto-renewal switched on.

steps.heading: Disable auto-renewal to stop future charges
steps.body: For a plan that should simply stop renewing, use the toggle switch on its row. Turning it off doesn't touch the service today: it keeps running until the current billing date, then expires without charging you again. For monthly plans specifically, disabling auto-renewal also voids any pending invoice for that service. Complex cases involving partially paid invoices or applied credit are better handled by contacting Hostinger support directly; don't guess at the toggle's effect there.

steps.heading: Cancel the subscription outright
steps.body: Want the service gone now instead of waiting for the billing period to run out? Open the row and use the Cancel subscription action. Hostinger's interface does not use a trash icon for this; cancellation is a labeled button, not a delete icon. If the plan still qualifies for Hostinger's refund window, cancelling through Paid Invoices and requesting a refund terminates the service immediately. Outside that window, cancelling stops the service at its existing expiration date, the same outcome as disabling auto-renewal. Either way, Hostinger deletes the service's files, databases, and email permanently once it's gone. Back up anything you need first.

steps.heading: Confirm the change stuck
steps.body: Refresh the Subscriptions page and check the row again. A cancelled plan should show its status changed and the auto-renewal toggle off; a fully terminated one should show as expired or disappear from the active list. If your real goal was just to stop being charged anywhere on the account, check Billing → Payment Methods too, since removing a card there is a second, separate safeguard on top of anything you changed at the subscription level.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no trash or delete icon on the subscription row
troubleshooting.cause: Hostinger's current billing interface doesn't offer a delete icon for services. The available actions are the auto-renewal toggle and, on eligible rows, a Cancel subscription button.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Cancel subscription to end the service, or the toggle to stop it renewing at the next billing date. There is no separate way to remove a row from the list before that.

troubleshooting.problem: Disabling auto-renewal didn't refund the last charge
troubleshooting.cause: Auto-renewal only prevents the next charge. It doesn't reverse a payment already taken, and outside Hostinger's refund window, cancelling doesn't either.
troubleshooting.fix: Check whether the service is still inside its refund window under Billing → Paid Invoices. If it is, request the refund there instead of just toggling auto-renewal.

troubleshooting.problem: Cancelled the wrong thing and lost data
troubleshooting.cause: Hostinger deletes a service's files, databases, and email permanently once it's cancelled or expires. There's no undo.
troubleshooting.fix: Contact Hostinger support immediately; recovery isn't guaranteed. For future cancellations, download a manual backup before confirming.

faq.question: Will canceling my Hostinger VPS stop future charges immediately?
faq.answer: Disabling auto-renewal stops the next charge, but the service itself keeps running until its existing billing date instead of shutting off instantly. Only a refund within Hostinger's refund window, or cancelling a service that's already outside any billing commitment, ends it right away.

faq.question: Is there a delete icon for removing a Hostinger service?
faq.answer: No. Hostinger's Subscriptions page uses an auto-renewal toggle and a Cancel subscription action, not a trash icon. Cancelling ends the row's active status; it doesn't erase the row from the page instantly.

faq.question: What does "pending setup" mean on a subscription row?
faq.answer: The order was started but never completed, so it hasn't provisioned. These rows show a button to finish the order instead of a billing date.

faq.question: Can I get a refund instead of just cancelling?
faq.answer: If the service is still within Hostinger's refund window, cancelling through Billing → Paid Invoices and requesting a refund ends it immediately. Outside that window, you can only stop it from renewing further.

faq.question: Can I delete shared hosting without closing my whole Hostinger account?
faq.answer: Yes. Each subscription is cancelled independently from Billing → Subscriptions, so other services and the account itself stay active.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in July 2025. Re-checked against Hostinger's official support documentation in September 2026: the earlier draft described a trash-can icon as the delete control, but Hostinger's current billing interface uses an auto-renewal toggle plus a labeled Cancel subscription action instead, and that correction is reflected throughout this version. The refund-window and pending-invoice behavior were also confirmed against the same documentation.
